clue.text: Jam slice

definitions.meaning: to jam something is to force it tightly into place
a slice of cake or cheese is a thick triangular piece

explanation.definitionFit: To jam a door is to wedge it, and a slice of cheese can be a wedge-shaped piece.

clue.text: Pinched part of vital statistics

parts.note: the middle measurement of bust, waist and hips, when drawn in very narrow like an insect's

explanation.definitionFit: A very slender middle, narrow as an insect's, is the tightest of the three body measurements.

clue.text: Type of shirt worn by European poet

indicators.note: the shirt is worn by, so inside, the European

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark
a T-shirt is a type of shirt, giving T

explanation.surface: A Continental writer wears a particular style of shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn by' puts T inside DANE, before its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of the Divine Comedy is the great Italian poet.

clue.text: Go abroad for the end of spring in Dubai, for example

indicators.note: the letter goes in the Gulf state word

parts.note: Dubai is one of the United Arab Emirates, an emirate

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone moves overseas to the Gulf for late spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of' picks the final letter of 'spring', and 'in' sets it inside the Gulf state word; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's country to settle in another.

clue.text: Tempers be frayed at this time of year

indicators.note: frayed tempers are ragged and worn, so these letters come apart and are rewoven

explanation.surface: People grow irritable at a certain point in the calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frayed' rearranges TEMPERSBE; 'this time of year' points to the month itself, with 'at' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth month is a particular time of year, so the phrase names it.

clue.text: Writer moved by desert storm

definitions.meaning: George ... was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin
what a storm in the desert whips up and carries

explanation.definitionFit: George Sand was a nineteenth-century novelist, and grains are blown about by a desert storm.

clue.text: One man with help could become outstanding

indicators.note: the letters could become another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: A single person with assistance might achieve greatness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could become' rearranges ONEMANHELP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extraordinary or remarkable is outstanding.

clue.text: Alone I panic, being windy

indicators.note: panicking throws these letters into disorder

explanation.surface: A lone person is frightened, getting nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'panic' rearranges ALONEI; 'windy' is also slang for scared, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeolus was the god of winds, so this adjective means relating to or caused by wind.

clue.text: Game of many hazards — winning and losing

definitions.text: Game of many hazards — winning and losing

parts.words: Game of many hazards — winning and losing
parts.note: reads like a risky gamble, but a winning hazard and a losing hazard are scoring strokes in a cue game

explanation.surface: A risky contest where fortunes rise and fall.
explanation.walkthrough: In this cue sport, potting the object ball is a winning hazard and potting your own ball off another is a losing hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: The table game played with three balls scores by strokes called winning and losing hazards.

clue.text: Diamonds boding ill for Kipling's lady

definitions.meaning: Kipling's poem The Liner, She's a Lady calls a ship a lady, and reefs spell danger for a ship

explanation.definitionFit: Slang calls diamonds rocks, and rocks ahead threaten a ship, which Kipling personified as a lady.

clue.text: Awareness that one is breaking a ruling

indicators.note: the numeral breaks into the ruling word, splitting it open

parts.note: a judge's ruling on a convicted person is a sentence
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone realises that an individual is defying an official decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is breaking' puts I inside SENTENCE, between its second N and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Being conscious and able to feel is a form of awareness.

clue.text: Colour for a garden shrub

definitions.meaning: a bush with fragrant purple or white blossom grown in gardens

explanation.definitionFit: The pale mauve colour is named after the flowering bush of the same name.

clue.text: To stray off course is within reason in a boat

indicators.note: the straying word sits within the reason word

parts.note: why means the reason for something
to err is to wander from the right path

explanation.surface: Wandering off course is understandable when you are out in a small craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is within' sets the straying word inside the reason word; 'in a' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A light rowing vessel used on rivers, or a barge, is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Successful defender in Italian bridge contest

definitions.text: Successful defender in Italian bridge contest

parts.words: Successful defender in Italian bridge contest
parts.note: reads like a card player defending a contract, but it is the Roman hero who held a bridge over the Tiber against the Etruscan army

explanation.surface: A player wins a card game tournament in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Roman legend, and in Macaulay's poem, Horatius Cocles held the Sublician bridge against Lars Porsena's army; 'bridge' is not the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Roman soldier who kept the bridge against the Etruscans fought off the attackers.

clue.text: Just the job for the seamstress we hear

indicators.note: signals that the words are heard, not read

parts.note: a seamstress could be called a tailor maid, a maid who sews

explanation.surface: Sewing would be the perfect work for a dressmaker, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: TAILOR MAID, a maid who sews, sounds like the phrase meaning perfectly suited.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made to measure fits exactly, so it is perfectly suited, exactly right.

clue.text: A fun date — it changed the state of Romeo and Juliet

definitions.text: the state of Romeo and Juliet

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: An enjoyable evening out transformed the famous young lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges AFUNDATEIT; the definition describes the lovesick condition of Shakespeare's pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo and Juliet were besotted, overcome with passion for each other.

clue.text: Standard weight of canvas for some artists?

parts.note: a standard is a banner or flag
a stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds

explanation.surface: Asks about the usual heaviness of painters' canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: Pavement artists draw in chalk on paving slabs; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Pavement artists draw on paving slabs, so a slab serves as their canvas.

clue.text: Prince in disguise as swordbearer

definitions.meaning: in the fairy tale, the enchanted prince is an amphibian until kissed
a loop on a belt that holds a sword or bayonet scabbard

explanation.definitionFit: The frog prince is a fairy-tale royal under a spell, and a frog is also a belt attachment carrying a scabbard.

clue.text: Mother perhaps under oath as sponsor

indicators.note: in a down clue the parent word is placed under the oath word

parts.note: God! is used as an oath
a mother is an example of a parent

explanation.surface: A mother swearing an oath to support someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A godparent stands sponsor at a baptism.
explanation.definitionFit: At a christening, a godparent acts as sponsor for the child.

clue.text: Doubly accomplished, but dried up

parts.note: over means finished, accomplished
done also means finished, accomplished, the second of the two

explanation.surface: Someone twice successful is nonetheless spent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubly' asks for two words meaning accomplished; 'dried up' describes food cooked too long.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat cooked too long becomes dry and shrivelled.

clue.text: He escapes the beam of light from the carrier

indicators.note: the pronoun escapes from the article, leaving it behind

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A man flees the light shining from some transport vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escapes' removes the pronoun from the article, leaving a single letter, which leads the beam word; 'carrier' means something you carry things on.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat board with a rim is used for carrying plates and cups.

clue.text: Poorly informed, being short-sighted

parts.note: poorly means unwell, ill
to be informed is to be advised

explanation.surface: Someone badly briefed proves to lack foresight.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Poorly informed' as one phrase with no comma, but it splits into two synonyms; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-sighted decision is unwise, lacking thought for the future.

clue.text: Odds on a fall creating injury

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds on a horse
a fall of rain

explanation.surface: Betting on a tumble that causes a wrench.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, the starting price, is the odds at the start of a horse race; 'on' places it above RAIN in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrenched ankle or wrist is a common injury.

clue.text: Take steps to exhibit document

parts.note: a pas is a step in ballet, the same word in the plural
to sport something is to wear or display it proudly

explanation.surface: Someone acts to put a piece of paperwork on show.
explanation.walkthrough: PAS is French for a step, used of dance steps; 'Take' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The travel paper issued by a government is an official document.

clue.text: President pressed button to cause damage

parts.note: one rang by pressing a bell button

explanation.surface: A head of state hits the button to wreak havoc.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for crashing a car or plane and damaging it.
explanation.definitionFit: To crash a vehicle is to prang it, informal British slang for damaging it in a collision.

clue.text: Trespass by amateur in war zone

parts.note: a trespass is a wrongdoing, an offence

explanation.surface: A non-professional intrudes onto a battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crimean peninsula was the scene of the 1850s war and of later conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Sea peninsula gave its name to the Crimean War, a famous battleground.

clue.text: Network includes unit for food

indicators.note: the network word includes the unit inside it

parts.note: a maze is a network of paths
I is one, a unit

explanation.surface: A system contains a component for nourishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' sets the unit inside the network word; 'for' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetcorn is a cereal crop eaten as food.

clue.text: Adds up to being one of the herd

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: The totals amount to membership of a group.
explanation.walkthrough: A stot is a young bullock, a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bullock is an animal in a cattle herd.

clue.text: In a romantic affair perfume is a must

indicators.note: the letters sit in the words of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: Scent is essential to a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'a romantic'; 'is a must' finishes the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant smell or scent is what a perfume gives off.

clue.text: License for a writer is essential at first

parts.note: an author is a writer
taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A permit for an author is vital from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'License' is the verb, US-style spelling, meaning to permit.
explanation.definitionFit: To license something is to give official permission for it.

clue.text: Signal to go at speed in restricted area

parts.note: a green light is the signal to go
to belt along is to go at speed

explanation.surface: A driver gets the go-ahead and races through a zone with limits.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a green belt is protected countryside around a city where building is restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: Countryside around a town where development is forbidden is a planning-restricted zone.

clue.text: Upright before the court

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: An honest person stands before the judges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something standing straight up is vertical, upright.
